deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a page of German lecture or study notes on ancient Egyptian history, continuing the previous page (folio 30). The previous page covers the earliest period, the castes after Herodotus, and the kings of Thebes and Memphis down to Sethos (c. 700 BC). The handwriting and content (school or university ancient-history notes in the style of Heeren-type lectures) suggest these are not Gauss's own mathematical papers. They are probably notes by a student or family member bound into the bundle.

Content of the page:
(1) After Sethos's death Egypt was divided among 12 rulers (the Dodecarchy). One of them, Psammetich, seized sole rule and became king over all Egypt.
(2) Heading: 'Zweite Periode. Von der Alleinherrschaft Psammetichs bis auf die persische Eroberung Aegyptens durch Cambyses, 660–525.'
(3) Narrative of this period:
- Psammetich won sole rule with the help of foreign troops. Driven out by the other rulers, he had fled to Lower Egypt. While he was there, Greek sea-raiders landed. He took them into his pay and defeated the other rulers.
- The warrior caste was offended by this, and a large number of warriors (Herodotus: 240,000) emigrated to Ethiopia.
- Psammetich tried to push into Asia but was held up for 29 years besieging the Philistine border fortress Asdod.
- The Scythian invasion of Western Asia (Vorderasien) falls in his reign.
- He died after a reign of 54 years and was succeeded by his son Neco.
- Neco carried out enterprising plans. He resolved to join [the Red Sea and] the Mediterranean by a canal; this sentence continues on the next page.

No derivation, computation or formula appears anywhere on the page.
errors: No mathematical errors are possible; the page is historical prose.

Historical content agrees with Herodotus Book II: the 12 kings, Psammetichus and the Ionian/Carian 'bronze men', 240,000 deserters to Ethiopia, the 29-year siege of Azotus, the 54-year reign, and Necho's canal plan.
The dates 660–525 are conventional approximations of the period. Psammetichus I reigned c. 664–610 BC, and the Persian conquest under Cambyses was 525 BC.

results.what: Narrative of Egyptian history from the Dodecarchy and Psammetichus I to Necho II (lecture notes)
results.modern_name: Saite (26th) Dynasty history after Herodotus II.147–158
results.usually_credited_to: Herodotus (source); standard early-19th-century German history textbooks/lectures

deep.surprise_reason: The page is non-mathematical history notes (ancient Egypt, Psammetichus to Necho) and very likely not by Gauss himself. It contains nothing of mathematical-historical significance.

checkable.asserts: Psammetichus I's reign of 54 years is consistent with the modern dates 664–610 BC.
The span of the 'Second Period' as dated in the heading (660–525) is 135 years.

transcription_corrections: Heading: read 'bis auf die persische Eroberung Aegyptens durch Cambyses' (the heading is underlined; 'Aegyptens' runs into 'durch').
'Psammetich versuchte[?] in Asien sich zu vergrößern[?]' more likely reads 'Psammetich versuchte in Asien ein zu dringen' (einzudringen).
'Unter Psammetich zog[?] auch fällt[?]' should likely read 'Unter Psammetichs Regierung fällt auch der Einbruch der Scythen in Vorderasien'.
The number of emigrating warriors is hard to read (240000 or 140000). Herodotus gives 240,000.
Near the end, 'Durch ihn ward[?] der Canal[?] zwar angelegt[?], führte aber unternehmende[?] Pläne[?] aus' is uncertain. The latter half plausibly reads 'führte aber mehrere merkwürdige Pläne aus'.
The last line probably reads 'Er faßte den Entschluß, das rothe [und das] mittländische Meer...', continuing onto the next page.
